The three regions already marked in the center are: R is above G, and O is to their right; on the far right there is a vertical region labeled X. Name them according to the method specified in the problem: the unmarked L-shaped region above and to the left of the central R, G, O is A; the horizontal strip below G and O is B; the vertical strip to the right of O and to the left of X is C; the upper and left L-shaped region in the further outer layer is D; the bottom outer horizontal strip is E. As can be seen from the figure, A touches R, G, O; B touches A, G, O; C touches A, B, O; D touches A, B, C; E touches B, C, D; X touches C, D, E. Reasoning: There are four colors R, G, O, Y, and adjacent touching regions have different colors. A touches the known R, G, O, so A can only be Y. B touches A=Y, G, O, so B can only be R. C touches A=Y, B=R, O, so C can only be G. D touches A=Y, B=R, C=G, so D can only be O. E touches B=R, C=G, D=O, so E can only be Y. Finally, X touches C=G, D=O, E=Y, so X can only be R, namely red.

From the image, A touches R, G, and O; B touches A, G, and O; C touches A, B, and O; D touches A, B, and C; E touches B, C, and D; and X touches C, D, and E. From the text, touching regions must have different colours among R, G, O, Y. Therefore A must be Y, B must be R, C must be G, D must be O, E must be Y, and finally X, touching G, O, and Y, must be R.
